experiment_name: FSFFL NEXT — D2 explicit career-state Intrinsic validation

candidates.A: PR #138 incumbent: discounted structurally relevant expected career production
candidates.C: smooth marginal franchise contribution using continuous Forecast uncertainty
candidates.D: first explicit career-state challenger with hard state-conditioned neutral contribution
candidates.D2: explicit career-state probabilities plus state-conditioned smooth neutral contribution; generic Forecast SD cannot move probability mass across states

recommendation: KEEP A. D2 is not promoted. It proves explicit-state option value can eliminate generic-variance-as-free-upside and fixes much of the within-state compression defect, but the current state taxonomy/transition probabilities are materially miscalibrated. The next work belongs in Forecast career-state calibration, especially RB/WR/TE. PR #138 remains unmerged.

key_metrics.comparison_target: D2 smooth realized neutral-format contribution target

current_player_sanity_summary.evaluation: measurement-only D2 sanity on governed current Forecast path
current_player_sanity_summary.headline: D2 fixes within-state compression but exposes state-model calibration problems; most named current players are classified elite.

comparisons.Judkins_vs_JSN: Judkins 120.48 > JSN 120.10 — essentially tied but still reversed from desired recurring sanity ordering
comparisons.KC_vs_Bowers: KC Concepcion 36.31 > Brock Bowers 32.79 — not coherent
comparisons.elite_QB_order: Josh Allen 141.22 > Drake Maye 98.19 > Lamar Jackson 90.31 > Dak Prescott 64.43 > Sam Darnold 40.34 — coherent
comparisons.within_state_compression: materially improved: first-generation D gave Pitts and McBride identical 6.54; D2 separates McBride 53.47, Bowers 32.79, Pitts 21.92 using player-specific current production plus bounded future states

major_defects: Career-state probabilities are under-calibrated upward (29.1% predicted vs 37.3% realized) and over-calibrated downward (33.7% vs 27.3%).
The six-state production taxonomy is too coarse in the current live sanity population: nearly all named high-usage players classify as elite, limiting meaningful role discrimination.
D2 loses to A in all 12 chronological folds, all four positions, young/developmental, prime, aging and fringe groups; it only improves the elite-tail MAE.
D2 remains materially worse than first-generation D on the common D2 target (34.87 vs 31.68 MAE), despite fixing within-state compression.
TE-premium scoring propagation remains a separate integration issue and was not repaired inside Intrinsic.
next_required_action: Do not create another Value transform. Keep A as the Intrinsic primitive. Improve Forecast-owned career-state taxonomy and transition calibration—especially RB/WR/TE upward development and role-loss probabilities—then rerun the exact frozen D2 experiment. Separately repair/verify TE-premium scoring propagation upstream of Intrinsic. Do not merge PR #138 without management approval.
